events.factual_description: Keystone Korner Baltimore and its authorized InstantSeats listing present Ami Taf Ra & Kamasi Washington on Tuesday, November 10, 2026 at 7:00 PM for a live presentation celebrating Taf Ra's debut album The Prophet and The Madman. InstantSeats describes the project as an ongoing creative collaboration between Taf Ra and Washington and states that the Washington-produced Brainfeeder album brings together Moroccan Gnawa, Arabic musical traditions, gospel, soul, and spiritual jazz. The authorized listing gives in-person face-value tickets at $55-$65 plus fees and a separate $20 streaming pass; Keystone Korner's venue information states that doors open at 5:00 PM for Tuesday-Thursday 7:00 PM shows. The venue calendar labels the project 'The Profit & The Madman,' but the authorized ticket description, Ami Taf Ra's official site, and Apple Music all verify the album title as The Prophet and The Madman. No backing musicians beyond Taf Ra and Washington are announced on the sources checked for this specific Baltimore date, so none are inferred.

en.why_it_matters: The reason to go is the project, not Washington's name by itself. Taf Ra's voice and North African musical vocabulary sit inside a record world she built with Washington, where Gnawa and Arabic traditions meet gospel, soul, spiritual jazz and his broad saxophone language. In Keystone Korner's small room, that cross-cultural architecture should register at human scale rather than as a festival-sized Kamasi set.
en.trip_verdict: From the DMV, I would actively make room for the Baltimore hop: this is the closest kind of room in which to hear the Taf Ra/Washington project take shape, and a single 7:00 PM set can anchor the night. I would not treat it as a scarcity chase because the collaboration is touring multiple US cities in November.

es.why_it_matters: La razón para ir es el proyecto, no el nombre de Washington por sí solo. La voz de Taf Ra y su vocabulario musical norteafricano viven dentro de un mundo discográfico que construyó con Washington, donde Gnawa y tradiciones árabes se cruzan con gospel, soul, spiritual jazz y el lenguaje amplio de su saxofón. En una sala pequeña como Keystone Korner, esa arquitectura intercultural debería sentirse a escala humana y no como un set de Kamasi pensado para festival.
es.trip_verdict: Desde el DMV sí haría espacio activamente para el brinco a Baltimore: es el tipo de sala cercana donde más sentido tiene escuchar cómo toma forma el proyecto Taf Ra/Washington, y el único set de las 7:00 PM puede sostener la noche. No lo trataría como persecución por escasez porque la colaboración está recorriendo varias ciudades de Estados Unidos en noviembre.
